text.en: Raju saw a farmer ripening bananas with a gas. "A plant hormone, ethylene!" said his teacher.

Hormones are chemical messengers made in small amounts. Plant hormones include auxins, which cause cell elongation; cytokinins, which promote cell division; gibberellins, which help stem growth; abscisic acid, a growth inhibitor; and ethylene, which ripens fruits.
In humans, hormones are made by the endocrine glands, which pour them directly into the blood. The pituitary is the master gland. The thyroid makes thyroxine, the parathyroid controls calcium, the pancreas makes insulin, the adrenal makes adrenaline and the gonads make sex hormones, while the thymus helps immunity.
Hormones must be balanced. Too little insulin causes diabetes and a lack of iodine can cause goitre by affecting the thyroid.
